about: What a person using Nourax Workspace must never see: the upstream name, links, logo or blue.
One source of truth for scripts/check-branding.sh (the guard), branding/audit/scan-page.js (the browser
audit) and the l10n sweep. See docs/branding.md.
Regex syntax must work in Python re, PHP PCRE (used with the u modifier) and JavaScript (with the u flag):
a pattern is case-sensitive, or starts with (?i) and has no other inline flag; no \x{...}, no possessive
quantifiers, no named groups, no ~ character. JSON escapes such as \u200c become the literal character.
Name patterns end without a word boundary, so endings like Nextcloudi or Nextcloudjához match too.
near_name is not a pattern but a distance check, for spellings nobody has listed yet.

note: Finds misspellings that no name pattern lists. A word of Latin letters (A-Z and U+00C0 to U+024F, not
right after another letter) names the upstream when one of its beginnings, min_length to max_length
letters long, is at most max_distance edits away from 'word', ignoring case. An edit adds, drops or
changes one letter, or swaps two letters next to each other (optimal string alignment distance). The
letters after that beginning are an ending, as in Nextcloudi; on a tie the longer beginning wins.
A scan of every translation of every app on the server (9543 .json and .js files, 2026-10-25) found nothing within
distance 2 that is not the name; at distance 3 'exclude' and 'de cloud' turn up, so keep it at 2.
The sweep replaces these words like the patterns above and lists them in --report, so they can be
added to latin-misspelt. Same code in lib/Service/L10nSweeper.php, scripts/check-branding.sh (its
Python and its PHP part) and branding/audit/scan-page.js.

about: How occ nourax_branding:sweep rewrites translations (lib/Service/L10nSweeper.php, docs/branding.md).
Each text goes through these steps in order: links to upstream addresses lose their address and keep their
text, bare upstream addresses are dropped, the phrases below run top to bottom, and then every name pattern
above (except the ones in generic_skip) becomes the product name.
These patterns are read by PHP only (PCRE with the u modifier); $1 in 'to' is the first group.
'langs' is 'en' (en, en_GB and other English variants), 'other' (every other language) or left out (all).

phrases.note: example cloud IDs such as user@your-nextcloud.org or felhasználó@az-ön-nextcloudja.org, in every language
the next rule, between two full stops
(Nextcloud <= 9): an old upstream version, nothing to say to people

the upstream company; its notices have curated texts in en-overrides.json, this only catches new ones
